name: Azure Well-Architected Reliability Assessment
completeness_scope: All 456 APRL recommendations from 83 source files at the pinned commit. The 393 active recommendations exactly match the object consumed by WARA v1.0.6; 63 disabled recommendations are retained for lifecycle completeness.

controls.title: Use replica sets for resiliency or geolocation in Microsoft Entra Domain Services
controls.description:
To improve the resiliency of a Microsoft Entra Domain Services managed domain, or deploy to additional geographic locations close to your applications, you can use replica sets.
You can add a replica set to any peered virtual network in any Azure region that supports Domain Services.

wara.potential_benefits: The replica sets provide geographical resiliency.
wara.learn_more_name: Create and use replica sets for resiliency or geolocation in Microsoft Entra Domain Services

controls.title: Use at least the Enterprise SKU
controls.description: You need to use a minimum of Enterprise SKU for your managed domain to support replica sets.

wara.potential_benefits: The Enterprise SKU enables creation of replica sets.
wara.learn_more_name: Create and use replica sets for resiliency or geolocation in Microsoft Entra Domain Services

controls.title: Enable Availability Zones on Premium API Management instances
controls.description: Zone redundancy for APIM instances ensures the gateway and control plane (Management API, developer portal, Git configuration) are replicated across datacenters in physically separated zones, boosting resilience to zone failures.

wara.learn_more_name: Ensure API Management availability and reliability

controls.title: Configure API management service in multiple Azure regions
controls.description: API Management multi-region deployment will help to reduce request latency perceived by geographically distributed API consumers and improves service availability if one region goes offline.

wara.potential_benefits: Improve latency and provides business continuity
wara.learn_more_name: Deploy API Management instance to multiple Azure regions

controls.title: Enable caching to improve performance in Azure API Management
controls.description: Response caching can significantly reduce latency for API callers and backend load for API providers.

wara.potential_benefits: Ensures service continuity and high availability
wara.learn_more_name: Add caching to improve performance in Azure API Management

controls.title: Migrate API Management services to Premium SKU to support Availability Zones
controls.description: Upgrading the API Management instance to the Premium SKU adds support for Availability Zones, enhancing availability and resilience by distributing services across physically separate locations within Azure regions.

wara.learn_more_name: Change your API Management service tier

controls.title: Enable auto-scale for production workloads on API Management services
controls.description: Use API Management with auto-scale for high availability in workloads that experience variable traffic patterns. There are several limitations with auto-scale, so review the documentation to ensure it meets your requirements.

wara.learn_more_name: Setting up auto-scale for Azure API Management

controls.title: Azure API Management platform version should be stv2
controls.description: stv1 instances were deprecated on August 31, 2024. If not migrated to stv2 by then, auto-migration will occur. In some cases, due to technical limitations, services may be shut down in March 2025.

wara.learn_more_name: Azure API Management - stv1 platform retirement (August 2024)

controls.title: Enable container health probes
controls.description: Enable container health probes to monitor the health of your container apps and ensure that unhealthy containers are restarted automatically.

wara.learn_more_name: Health probes for Azure Container Apps

controls.title: Deploy zone redundant Container app environments
controls.description: To take advantage of availability zones, you must enable zone redundancy when you create a Container Apps environment. The environment must include a virtual network with an available subnet. To ensure proper distribution of replicas, set your app's minimum replica count to three.

controls.title: Upgrade to App Configuration Standard tier
controls.description: SLA is not available for Free tier. Upgrade to the Standard tier to get an SLA of 99.9%

wara.potential_benefits: High availability, more storage, higher request quota.

controls.title: Enable Purge protection for Azure App Configuration
controls.description: With Purge protection enabled, soft deleted stores can't be purged in the retention period. If disabled, the soft deleted store can be purged before the retention period expires.

wara.potential_benefits: Prevent accidental deletion of configuration stores.

controls.title: Set up disaster recovery of Automation accounts and its dependent resources
controls.description: Set up disaster recovery for Automation accounts and resources like Modules, Connections, Credentials, Certificates, Variables, and Schedules to deal with region or zone failures. A replica Automation account should be ready in a secondary region for failover.

controls.title: Monitor Memory Utilization to ensure sufficient resources for workloads
controls.description: Ensure sufficient memory resources to prevent host resource exhaustion in Azure VMware Solution. It uses vSphere DRS and vSphere HA for dynamic workload management. Yet, continuous memory use over 95% leads to disk swapping, affecting workloads.

controls.title: Monitor when Azure VMware Solution Private Cloud is reaching the capacity limit
controls.description: Set an alert for when the node count in Azure VMware Solution Private Cloud hits or exceeds 90 hosts, enabling timely planning for a new private cloud.

controls.title: Configure Azure Monitor Alert warning thresholds for vSAN datastore utilization
controls.description: Ensure VMware vSAN datastore slack space is maintained for SLA by monitoring storage utilization and setting alerts at 70% and 75% utilization to allow for capacity planning. To expand, add hosts or external storage like Azure Elastic SAN, Azure NetApp Files, if CPU and RAM requirements are met.

controls.title: Monitor CPU Utilization to ensure sufficient resources for workloads
controls.description: Ensure sufficient compute resources to avoid host resource exhaustion in Azure VMware Solution, which utilizes vSphere DRS and HA for dynamic workload resource management. However, sustained CPU utilization over 95% may increase CPU Ready times, impacting workloads.

controls.title: Configure Azure Service Health notifications and alerts for Azure VMware Solution
controls.description: Ensure Azure Service Health notifications are set for Azure VMware Solution across all used regions and subscriptions. This communicates service/security issues and maintenance activities like host replacements and upgrades, reducing service request submissions.

controls.title: Enable Stretched Clusters for Multi-AZ Availability of the vSAN Datastore
controls.description: For Azure VMware Solution, enabling Stretched Clusters offers 99.99% SLA, synchronous storage replication (RPO=0), and spreads vSAN datastore across two AZs. Must be done at initial setup, needing double quota due to extension across AZs.

controls.title: Apply Resource delete lock on the resource group hosting the private cloud
controls.description: Applying a resource delete lock to the Azure VMware Solution Private Cloud resource group prevents unauthorized or accidental deletion by anyone with contributor access, ensuring the protection and reliability of the Azure VMware Solution Private Cloud.

wara.learn_more_name: Lock your resources to protect your infrastructure

controls.title: Use key autorotation for vSAN datastore customer-managed keys
controls.description: When using customer-managed keys for encrypting vSAN datastores, leveraging Azure Key Vault for central management and accessing them via a managed identity linked to the private cloud is advised. The expiration of these keys can render the vSAN datastore and its associated workloads inaccessible.

controls.title: Monitor when Azure VMware Solution Cluster Size is approaching the host limit
controls.description: Alert when the cluster size reaches 14 hosts. Set up periodic alerts for planning new clusters or datastores due to growth, especially from storage needs. Beyond 14 hosts, trigger alerts for each new host addition for proactive resource monitoring.

controls.title: Configure Syslog in Diagnostic Settings for Azure VMware Solution
controls.description: Ensure Diagnostic Settings are configured for each private cloud to send syslogs to external sources for analysis and/or archiving. Azure VMware Solution Syslogs contain data for troubleshooting and performance, aiding quicker issue resolution and early detection of issues.

controls.title: Use multiple DNS servers per private FQDN zone
controls.description: Azure VMware Solution private clouds support up to three DNS servers for a single FQDN, preventing a single DNS server from becoming a point of failure. It's crucial to use multiple DNS servers for on-premises FQDN resolution from each private cloud.

controls.title: Monitor Batch Account quota
controls.description: To ensure cross-region disaster recovery and business continuity, set the right quotas for all Batch accounts to allocate necessary core numbers upfront, preventing execution interruptions from reaching quota limits.

controls.title: Create an Azure Batch pool across Availability Zones
controls.description: When using Virtual Machine Configuration for Azure Batch pools, opting to distribute your pool across Availability Zones bolsters your compute nodes against Azure datacenter failures.

controls.title: Enable zone redundancy for Azure Cache for Redis
controls.description: Azure Cache for Redis offers zone redundancy in Premium and Enterprise tiers, using VMs across multiple Availability Zones to ensure greater resilience and availability.

wara.learn_more_name: Enable zone redundancy for Azure Cache for Redis

controls.title: Configure Private Endpoints
controls.description: Use private endpoints for secure connection to cache via a private link, avoiding the public internet.

wara.potential_benefits: Secure, private VNet ingress, efficient data transfer
wara.learn_more_name: Configure private endpoints for Azure Redis Cache

controls.title: Schedule updates by setting a maintenance window
controls.description: Azure Cache for Redis allows for specifying maintenance windows. A maintenance window allows you to control the days and times of a week during which the VMs hosting your cache can be updated.

controls.title: Configure logs
controls.description: Front Door logs offer comprehensive telemetry on each request, crucial for understanding your solution's performance and responses, especially when caching is enabled, as origin servers might not receive every request.

wara.learn_more_name: Monitor metrics and logs in Azure Front Door

controls.title: Enable the WAF
controls.description: For internet-facing applications, enabling the Front Door web application firewall (WAF) and configuring it to use managed rules is recommended for protection against a wide range of attacks using Microsoft-managed rules.

wara.learn_more_name: Web Application Firewall on Azure Front Door

controls.title: Secure your Origin with Private Link in Azure Front Door
controls.description: Azure Private Link enables secure access to Azure PaaS and services over a private endpoint in your virtual network, ensuring traffic goes over the Microsoft backbone network, not the public internet.

wara.learn_more_name: Private link for Azure Front Door

controls.title: Use HTTP to HTTPS redirection
controls.description: Using HTTPS is ideal for secure connections. However, for compatibility with older clients, HTTP requests may be necessary. Azure Front Door enables auto redirection of HTTP to HTTPS, enhancing security without sacrificing accessibility.

wara.learn_more_name: Create HTTP to HTTPS redirect rule

controls.title: Use managed TLS certificates
controls.description: When Front Door manages your TLS certificates, it reduces your operational costs and helps you to avoid costly outages caused by forgetting to renew a certificate. Front Door automatically issues and rotates the managed TLS certificates.

wara.learn_more_name: Configure HTTPS on an Azure Front Door custom domain using the Azure portal

controls.title: Disable health probes when there is only one origin in an origin group
controls.description: Front Door health probes help detect unavailable or unhealthy origins, directing traffic to alternate origins if needed.

controls.title: Use latest version for customer-managed certificates
controls.description: If you use your own TLS certificates, set the Key Vault certificate version to 'Latest' to avoid reconfiguring Azure Front Door for new certificate versions and waiting for deployment across Front Door's environments.

wara.potential_benefits: Saves time and automates TLS updates
wara.learn_more_name: Select the certificate for Azure Front Door to deploy

controls.title: Select good health probe endpoints
controls.description: Consider selecting a webpage or location specifically designed for health monitoring as the endpoint for Azure Front Door's health probes. This should encompass the status of critical components like application servers, databases, and caches to serve production traffic efficiently.

controls.title: Use the latest API version and SDK version
controls.description: When working with Azure Front Door through APIs, ARM templates, Bicep, or SDKs, using the latest API or SDK version is crucial. Updates bring new functions, important security patches, and bug fixes.

controls.title: Monitor Web Application Firewall
controls.description: Monitoring the health of your Web Application Firewall and the applications it protects is crucial. This can be achieved through integration with Microsoft Defender for Cloud, Azure Monitor, and Azure Monitor logs, ensuring optimal performance and security.

controls.title: Use HEAD health probes
controls.description: Health probes in Azure Front Door can use GET or HEAD HTTP methods. Using the HEAD method for health probes is a recommended practice because it reduces the traffic load on your origins, being less resource-intensive.

wara.learn_more_name: Supported HTTP methods for health probes

controls.title: Avoid using Classic Azure Front Door
controls.description: Azure Front Door standard is ~45% cheaper then AFD classic and has many additional benefits. Classic is also scheduled to be retired on March 31, 2027.

wara.potential_benefits: Costs savings and additional supported features
wara.learn_more_name: Compare pricing between Azure Front Door tiers

controls.title: Use geo-filtering in Azure Front Door
controls.description: Azure Front Door's geo-filtering through WAF enables defining custom access rules by country/region to restrict or allow web app access.

controls.title: Use the same domain name on Front Door and your origin
controls.description: Front Door can rewrite Host headers for custom domain names routing to a single origin, useful for avoiding custom domain configuration at both Front Door and the origin.

wara.learn_more_name: Preserve the original HTTP host name between a reverse proxy and its back-end web application

controls.title: Use end-to-end TLS
controls.description: Front Door terminates TCP and TLS connections from clients and establishes new connections from each PoP to the origin. Securing these connections with TLS, even for Azure-hosted origins, ensures data is always encrypted during transit.

wara.learn_more_name: End-to-end TLS with Azure Front Door

controls.title: Leverage Global provisioned deployment to ensure high and predictable throughput
controls.description: Global provisioned deployments provide reserved model processing capacity for high and predictable throughput using Azure global infrastructure. Suitable for applications requiring lower latency variance at large workload usage. Provides cost savings.

wara.potential_benefits: Low latency variance, high throughputs, business continuity

controls.title: Ensure PAYG AOAI models leverage Global Standard deployment
controls.description: Global Standard leverages Azure's global infrastructure to route traffic to the best available data center for customer's real-time inference requests. It provides the highest default quota and eliminates the need to load balance across multiple resources. Optimized for low to medium volume usage.

controls.title: Deploy a PAYG instance of the model with provisioned throughput to manage overflow effectively
controls.description: Provisioned Throughput offers pre-allocated capacity for consistent workloads, while Pay-as-You-Go charges for actual usage, ideal for variable workloads. During overflow, the Pay-as-You-Go instance manages excess load, ensuring service efficiency.

wara.potential_benefits: PAYG model balances cost and performance and helps scale

controls.title: Deploy AOAI Service in multiple regions using Standard and/or Provisioned deployments
controls.description: If your service needs to always be available, design AOAI Service to either failover into another region or split the workload between two or more regions. Applications requiring high degrees of resiliency should consider this to strengthen their model infrastructure.

wara.potential_benefits: Ensures business continuity during regional outages.

controls.title: Use comprehensive monitoring solution for AOAI service
controls.description: Implementing a comprehensive monitoring solution for AOAI involves using Azure Monitor to track API usage, performance metrics, and security events. This setup helps optimize performance, manage costs, and ensure compliance by providing detailed insights into model usage and potential issues.

wara.potential_benefits: Optimize performance and compliance with detailed insights

controls.title: Ensure that models are deployed using Global batch for large scale processing
controls.description: Global batch efficiently handles large-scale tasks within 24 hours. Submit requests in a single file, with a separate quota to protect online workloads. Key uses: data processing, content generation, document review, customer support automation, data extraction, NLP tasks, and marketing.

wara.potential_benefits: Cost effective faster turnaround for large-scale processing.

controls.title: Ensure AOAI models are deployed using Data Zone Standard for data residency requirements
controls.description: Data zone deployments route customer traffic to the highest availability data center within the defined data zone, ensuring data at rest remains within the Azure OpenAI resource geography. This approach offers increased quota limits and ensures data processing occurs within the specified data zone.

wara.potential_benefits: Enforce data residency and compliance standards

controls.title: Shared disks should only be enabled in clustered servers
controls.description: Azure shared disks let you attach a disk to multiple VMs at once for deploying or migrating clustered applications, suitable only when a disk is shared among VM cluster members.

controls.title: Use Azure Disks with Zone Redundant Storage for higher resiliency and availability
controls.description: Azure disks offers a zone-redundant storage (ZRS) option for workloads that need to be resilient to an entire zone being down. Due to the cross-zone data replication, ZRS disks have higher write latency when compared to the locally-redundant option (LRS), so make sure to benchmark your disks.

controls.title: Consider creating TrustedLaunchSupported images where possible
controls.description: We recommend creating Trusted Launch Supported Images for benefits like Secure Boot, vTPM, trusted launch VMs, large boot volume. These are Gen 2 Images by default and you cannot change a VM's generation after creation, so review the considerations first.

controls.title: Zone redundant storage should be used for image versions
controls.description: Use ZRS for high availability when creating image/VM versions in Azure Compute Gallery, offering resilience against Availability Zone failures. ZRS accounts are advisable in regions with Availability Zones, with the choice of Standard_ZRS recommended over Standard_LRS for these regions.

controls.title: Create Image Versions replicas in secondary region
controls.description: On multi-region deployments, replicate Image Versions to a secondary region to ensure disaster recovery capability. This ensures that the Image Versions are available in the secondary region in case of a disaster in the primary region.

controls.title: Configure Image version replica count per region.
controls.description: You can set a different replica count in each target region, based on the scale needs for the region. For every 20 VMs that you create concurrently, we recommend you keep one replica.

controls.title: A minimum of three replicas should be kept for production image versions
controls.description: Keeping a minimum of 3 replicas for production images in Azure's Compute Gallery ensures scalability and prevents throttling in multi-VM deployments by distributing VM deployments across different replicas. This reduces the risk of overloading a single replica.

controls.title: Use Managed Disks for VM disks
controls.description: Azure is retiring unmanaged disks on September 30, 2025. Users should plan the migration to avoid disruptions and maintain service reliability.

wara.learn_more_name: Migrate your Azure unmanaged disks by Sep 30, 2025

controls.title: Backup VMs with Azure Backup service
controls.description: Enable backups for your virtual machines with Azure Backup to secure and quickly recover your data. This service offers simple, secure, and cost-effective solutions for backing up and recovering data from the Microsoft Azure cloud.

wara.learn_more_name: What is the Azure Backup service?

controls.title: Run production workloads on two or more VMs using VMSS Flex
controls.description: Production VM workloads should be deployed on multiple VMs and grouped in a VMSS Flex instance to intelligently distribute across the platform, minimizing the impact of platform faults and updates.

wara.learn_more_name: What has changed with Flexible orchestration mode

controls.title: Deploy VMs across Availability Zones
controls.description: Azure Availability Zones, within each Azure region, are tolerant to local failures, protecting applications and data against unlikely Datacenter failures by being physically separate.

wara.learn_more_name: Create virtual machines in an availability zone using the Azure portal

controls.title: Enable Scheduled Events for Maintenance sensitive workload VMs
controls.description: If your workload is Maintenance sensitive, enable Scheduled Events. This Azure Metadata Service lets your app prepare for virtual machine maintenance by providing information on upcoming events like reboots, reducing disruptions.

wara.learn_more_name: Monitor scheduled events for your Azure VMs

controls.title: Reserve Compute Capacity for critical workloads
controls.description: Azure Capacity Reservations ensure high availability for virtual machines by reserving compute capacity in advance within a specific region or availability zone. This guarantees that VMs will have the necessary resources during peak demand or maintenance events, enhancing reliability and uptime.

controls.title: Don't use A or B-Series VMs for production needing constant full CPU performance
controls.description: A-series VMs are tailored for entry-level workloads like development and testing, including use cases such as development and test servers, low traffic web servers, and small to medium databases.

wara.potential_benefits: Ensures full CPU usage for heavy tasks

controls.title: IP Forwarding should only be enabled for Network Virtual Appliances
controls.description: IP forwarding allows a virtual machine network interface to receive and send network traffic not destined for or originating from its assigned IP addresses.

controls.title: Host database data on a data disk
controls.description: A data disk is a managed disk attached to a virtual machine for storing database or other essential data. These disks are SCSI drives labeled as per choice.

wara.learn_more_name: Introduction to Azure managed disks - Data disks

controls.title: Use maintenance configurations for the Dedicated and/or Isolated VM SKUs
controls.description: The maintenance configuration settings let users schedule and manage updates, making sure the updates or interruptions on the VM are performed within a planned timeframe.

wara.learn_more_name: Use maintenance configurations to control and manage the VM updates

controls.title: Reserve Compute Capacity in Disaster Recovery Regions
controls.description: On-Demand Capacity Reservations ensure recovery of virtual machines in the event of a natural disaster by reserving compute capacity in advance within a specific region or zone. This guarantees that VMs have the necessary resources during disaster recovery failover events thus reducing downtime.

wara.potential_benefits: Guaranteed capacity in disaster recovery regions

controls.title: Update the Azure Linux VM Agent
controls.description: If you've installed the Azure Linux Agent or are using an endorsed distribution image, ensure your agent version is up-to-date. Some Linux distributions may disable auto-update or use older agent versions.

wara.learn_more_name: How to update the Azure Linux Agent on a VM

controls.title: Network access to the VM disk should be set to Disable public access and enable private access
controls.description: Recommended changing to "Disable public access and enable private access" and creating a Private Endpoint to improve security by restricting direct public access and ensuring connections are made privately, enhancing data protection and minimizing potential external threats.

wara.learn_more_name: Restrict import/export access for managed disks using Azure Private Link

controls.title: When AccelNet is enabled, you must manually update the GuestOS NIC driver
controls.description: When Accelerated Networking is enabled, the default Azure VNet interface in GuestOS is swapped for a Mellanox, and its driver comes from a 3rd party. Marketplace images have the latest Mellanox drivers, but post-deployment, updating the driver is the user's responsibility.

controls.title: Use Azure Boost VMs for Maintenance sensitive workload VMs
controls.description: If the workload is Maintenance sensitive, consider Azure Boost compatible VMs. Azure Boost is designed to lessen the impact on customers when Azure maintenance activities occur on the host.

controls.title: Migrate VMs using availability sets to VMSS Flex
controls.description: While availability sets are not scheduled for immediate deprecation, they are planned to be deprecated in the future. Migrate workloads from VMs to VMSS Flex for deployment across zones or within the same zone across different fault domains (FDs) for better reliability.

wara.learn_more_name: Migrate deployments and resources to Virtual Machine Scale Sets in Flexible orchestration

controls.title: Enable VM Insights
controls.description: VM Insights monitors VM and scale set performance, health, running processes, and dependencies. It enhances the predictability of application performance and availability by pinpointing performance bottlenecks and network issues, and it clarifies if problems are related to other dependencies.

controls.title: Replicate VMs using Azure Site Recovery
controls.description: Replicating Azure VMs via Site Recovery entails continuous, asynchronous disk replication to a target region. Recovery points are generated every few minutes, ensuring a Recovery Point Objective (RPO) in minutes.

controls.title: Mission Critical Workloads should consider using Premium or Ultra Disks
controls.description: Compared to Standard HDD and SSD, Premium SSD, SSD v2, and Ultra Disks offer improved performance, configurability, and higher single-instance VM uptime SLAs. The lowest SLA of all disks on a VM applies, so it is best to use Premium or Ultra Disks for the highest uptime SLA.

wara.potential_benefits: Enhanced performance, cost efficiency, and uptime SLA
wara.learn_more_name: Disk type comparison and decision tree

controls.title: Enable Accelerated Networking (AccelNet)
controls.description: Accelerated networking enables SR-IOV to a VM, greatly improving its networking performance by bypassing the host from the data path, which reduces latency, jitter, and CPU utilization for demanding network workloads on supported VM types.

wara.potential_benefits: Reduces latency, jitter and CPU use

controls.title: Deploy VMSS across availability zones with VMSS Flex
controls.description: When creating VMSS, implement availability zones as a protection measure for your applications and data against the rare event of datacenter failure.

wara.learn_more_name: Create a Virtual Machine Scale Set that uses Availability Zones

controls.title: Enable Predictive autoscale and configure at least for Forecast Only
controls.description: Predictive autoscale utilizes machine learning to efficiently manage and scale Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets by forecasting CPU load through historical usage analysis, ensuring timely scale-out to meet demand.

wara.learn_more_name: Use predictive autoscale to scale out before load demands in virtual machine scale sets

controls.title: Enable Automatic Repair Policy on Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets
controls.description: Enabling automatic instance repairs in Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets enhances application availability through a continuous health check and maintenance process.

wara.learn_more_name: Automatic instance repairs for Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets

controls.title: Upgrade VMSS Image versions scheduled to be deprecated or already retired
controls.description: Ensure current versions of images are in use to avoid disruption after image deprecation. Please review the publisher, offer, sku information of the VM to ensure you are running on a supported image. Enable Auto Guest Patching or Image Upgrades, to get notifications about image deprecation.

wara.potential_benefits: Avoid disruptions by updating VMSS images.

controls.title: Enable Azure Virtual Machine Scale Set Application Health Monitoring
controls.description: Monitoring application health in Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets is crucial for deployment management. It supports rolling upgrades such as automatic OS-image upgrades and VM guest patching, leveraging health monitoring for upgrading.

wara.learn_more_name: Using Application Health extension with Virtual Machine Scale Sets

controls.title: Use Ephemeral OS Disks for AKS VMSS Node Pools
controls.description: Ephemeral OS disks on AKS offer lower read/write latency due to local attachment, eliminating the need for replication seen with managed disks. This enhances performance and speeds up cluster operations such as scaling or upgrading due to quicker re-imaging and boot times.

wara.potential_benefits: Lower latency, faster re-imaging and booting

controls.title: Disable Force strictly even balance across zones to avoid scale in and out fail attempts
controls.description: Microsoft advises disabling strictly even VM instance distribution across Availability Zones in VMSS to improve scalability and flexibility, noting that uneven distribution may better serve application load demands despite the potential trade-off in resilience.

wara.learn_more_name: Use scale-in policies with Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets

controls.title: Set Patch orchestration options to Azure-orchestrated
controls.description: Enabling automatic VM guest patching eases update management by safely, automatically patching virtual machines to maintain security compliance, while limiting blast radius of VMs. Note, the KQL will not return sets using Uniform orchestration.

wara.learn_more_name: Automatic VM Guest Patching for Azure VMs

controls.title: Deploy VMSS with Flex orchestration mode instead of Uniform
controls.description: Deploying even single instance VMs into a scale set with Flexible orchestration mode future-proofs applications for scaling and availability. This mode guarantees high availability (up to 1000 VMs) by distributing VMs across fault domains in a region or within an Availability Zone.

wara.learn_more_name: When to use VMSS instead of VMs

controls.title: Configure VMSS Autoscale to custom and configure the scaling metrics
controls.description: Use custom autoscale for VMSS based on metrics and schedules to improve performance and cost effectiveness, adjusting instances as demand changes.

wara.learn_more_name: Get started with autoscale in Azure

controls.title: Disable anonymous pull access
controls.description: By default, Azure container registry requires authentication for pull/push actions. Enabling anonymous pull access exposes all content for public read actions. This applies to all repositories, potentially allowing unrestricted access if repository-scoped tokens are used.

controls.title: Create container registries with geo-replication enabled
controls.description: Use Azure Container Registry's geo-replication for multi-region deployments to simplify registry management and minimize latency. It enables serving global customers from local data centers and supports distributed development teams. Regional webhooks can notify of events in replicas.

controls.title: Manage registry size
controls.description: The storage constraints of Azure Container Registry's service tiers align with usage scenarios: Basic for starters, Standard for production, and Premium for high-scale performance and geo-replication.

wara.learn_more_name: Registry best practices - Manage registry size

controls.title: Configure Diagnostic Settings for all Azure Container Registries
controls.description: Resource Logs are not collected and stored until you create a diagnostic setting and route them to one or more locations.

wara.learn_more_name: Monitor Azure Container Registry - Enable diagnostic logs

controls.title: Enable zone redundancy
controls.description: Azure Container Registry's optional zone redundancy enhances resiliency and high availability for registries or replication resources in a specific region by distributing resources across multiple zones.

wara.learn_more_name: Registry best practices - Enable zone redundancy

controls.title: Move Container Registry to a dedicated resource group
controls.description: Container registries, used across multiple hosts, should be in their own resource group to prevent accidental deletion of images when container instances are deleted, preserving the image collection while experimenting with hosts.

wara.learn_more_name: Registry best practices - Use dedicated resource group

controls.title: Use Repository namespaces
controls.description: Using repository namespaces allows a single registry to be shared across multiple groups and deployments within an organization, supporting nested namespaces for group isolation. However, repositories are managed independently, not hierarchically.

wara.learn_more_name: Registry best practices - use repository namespaces

controls.title: Monitor Azure Container Registry with Azure Monitor
controls.description: Monitoring Azure resources using Azure Monitor enhances their availability, performance, and operation. Azure Container Registry, a full-stack monitoring service, provides features for Azure and other cloud and on-premises resources.

controls.title: Enable soft delete policy
controls.description: Enabling soft delete preview feature in Azure Container Registry (ACR) allows for the management of deleted artifacts with a specified retention period. Users can list, filter, and restore these artifacts until automatically purged post-retention.

controls.title: Use Premium tier for critical production workloads
controls.description: Choose a service tier of Azure Container Registry to meet your performance needs. Premium offers the most bandwidth and highest rate of read and write operations for high-volume deployments. Use Basic to start, Standard for production, and Premium for hyper-scale performance and geo-replication.

controls.title: Configure user nodepool count
controls.description: Configuring the user node pool with at least two nodes is essential for applications needing high availability, ensuring they remain operational and accessible without interruption.

wara.learn_more_name: Azure Well-Architected Framework review for Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)

controls.title: Update AKS tier to Standard or Premium
controls.description: Production AKS clusters require the Standard or Premium tier for a financially backed SLA and enhanced node scalability, as the free service lacks these features. Use the Premium tier for mission-critical workloads.

controls.title: Back up Azure Kubernetes Service
controls.description: AKS, popular for stateful apps needing backups, can now use Azure Backup to secure clusters and attached volumes through an installed Backup Extension, enabling backup and restore operations via a Backup Vault.

controls.title: Enable and remediate Azure Policies configured for AKS
controls.description: Azure Policies in AKS clusters help enforce governance best practices concerning security, authentication, provisioning, networking, and more, ensuring a robust and secure environment for operations.

controls.title: Deploy AKS cluster across availability zones
controls.description: Azure Availability Zones ensure high availability by offering independent locations within regions, equipped with their own power, cooling, and networking to ensure applications and data are protected from datacenter-level failures.

controls.title: Isolate system and application pods
controls.description: AKS assigns the kubernetes.azure.com/mode: system label to nodes in system node pools signaling the preference for system pods should be scheduled there. The CriticalAddonsOnly=true:NoSchedule taint can be added to your system nodes to prohibit application pods from being scheduled on them.

controls.title: Enable GitOps when using DevOps frameworks
controls.description: GitOps, an operating model for cloud-native apps, uses Git for storing application and infrastructure code as a source of truth for continuous delivery.

controls.title: Configure system nodepool count
controls.description: The system node pool should be configured with a minimum node count of three to ensure critical system pods are resilient to node outages.

controls.title: Enable the cluster auto-scaler on an existing cluster
controls.description: The cluster auto-scaler in AKS adjusts node counts based on pod resource needs and available capacity, enabling scaling as per demand to prevent outages.

wara.learn_more_name: Use the Cluster Autoscaler on AKS

controls.title: Deploy at least two replicas of your application
controls.description: Deploying at least two replicas of your application ensures that your application is highly available and can tolerate node failures.

controls.title: Use pod topology spread constraints to ensure that pods are spread across different nodes or zones
controls.description: Enhance availability and reliability by using pod topology spread constraints to control pod distribution based on node or zone topology, ensuring pods are spread across your cluster.

wara.potential_benefits: Ensures high availability and efficient use

controls.title: Implement Resource Quota to ensure that Kubernetes resources do not exceed hard resource limits
controls.description: A ResourceQuota object sets limits on resource use per namespace, controlling the number and type of objects created, and the total compute resources available.

wara.potential_benefits: Limits AKS resource usage per namespace

controls.title: Subscription core quota should be increased if Node pool auto-scale settings exceed the quota
controls.description: Node pool settings should not exceed the subscription core quota to ensure AKS can scale out nodes efficiently, meeting increased demand while reducing resource constraints and potential service disruptions.

controls.title: Configure pod disruption budgets (PDBs)
controls.description: A Pod Disruption Budget is a Kubernetes resource configuring the minimum number or percentage of pods that should remain available during disruptions like maintenance or scaling, ensuring a minimum number of pods are always available in the cluster.

controls.title: Upgrade Persistent Volumes using in-tree drivers to Azure CSI drivers
controls.description: From Kubernetes 1.26, Azure Disk and Azure File in-tree drivers are deprecated in favor of CSI drivers. Existing deployments remain operational but untested; users should switch to CSI drivers for new features and SKUs.

controls.title: Attach Virtual Nodes (ACI) to the AKS cluster
controls.description: To rapidly scale AKS workloads, utilize virtual nodes for quick pod provisioning, unlike Kubernetes auto-scaler. For clusters with availability zones, ensure one nodepool per AZ due to persistent volumes not working across AZs, preventing auto-scaler pod creation failures if lacking access.

controls.title: Use deployments with multiple replicas in production applications to guarantee availability
controls.description: Configuring multiple replicas in Pod or Deployment manifests stabilizes the number of replica Pods, ensuring that a specified number of identical Pods are always available, thereby guaranteeing their availability.

controls.title: Configure Azure CNI networking for dynamic allocation of IPs or use CNI overlay
controls.description: Azure CNI enhances cluster IP and network management, allowing dynamic IP allocation, scalable subnets, direct pod-VNET connectivity, and supports diverse network policies for pods and nodes with Azure Network Policies and Calico, optimizing network efficiency and security

wara.potential_benefits: Dynamic IP allocation, scalable subnets, direct VNET access

controls.title: Disable local accounts
controls.description: Local Kubernetes accounts in AKS, being non-auditable and legacy, are discouraged. Microsoft Entra's integration offers centralized management, multi-factor authentication, RBAC for detailed access, and a secure, scalable authentication system compatible with Azure and external identity providers.

controls.title: Configures Pods Liveness, Readiness, and Startup Probes
controls.description: AKS kubelet controller uses liveness probes to validate containers and applications health, ensuring the system knows when to restart a container based on its health status.

controls.title: Use zone-redundant storage for persistent volumes when running multi-zone AKS
controls.description: ZRS ensures data replication across three zones, protecting against zonal outages. It's available for Azure Disks, Container Storage, Files, and Blob by setting the SKU to ZRS in storage classes, enhancing multi-zone AKS clusters from v1.29.

controls.title: Enable AKS Monitoring
controls.description: Azure Monitor enables real-time health and performance insights for AKS by collecting events, capturing container logs, and gathering CPU/Memory data from the Metrics API. It allows data visualization using Azure Monitor Container Insights, Prometheus, Grafana, or others.

controls.title: Nodepool subnet size needs to accommodate maximum auto-scale settings
controls.description: Nodepool subnets sized for max auto-scale settings enable AKS to efficiently scale out nodes, meeting increased demand while reducing resource constraints and potential service disruptions.

controls.title: Use Azure Linux for Linux nodepools
controls.description: Azure Linux on AKS boosts resiliency with a native image using validated, source-built components. It's lightweight, reducing the attack surface and maintenance. A Microsoft-hardened kernel, optimized for Azure, enhances stability and security for container workloads.

controls.title: Enable zone redundancy in Managed Grafana
controls.description: Managed Grafana Standard tier is hosted on a dedicated set of VMs to provide redundancy. With zone redundancy enabled, VMs are spread across availability zones (AZ). Related resources are also configured for AZ. Zone redundancy can only be enabled when creating the Azure Managed Grafana instance.

wara.potential_benefits: Enhanced Managed Grafana resilience to failures
wara.learn_more_name: Enable zone redundancy in Azure Managed Grafana

controls.title: Define alternate VM SKUs
controls.description: Azure Databricks planning should include VM SKU swap strategies for capacity issues. VMs are regional, and allocation failures may occur, shown by a "CLOUD PROVIDER" error.

controls.title: Databricks runtime version is not latest or is not LTS version
controls.description: Databricks recommends migrating workloads to the latest or LTS version of its runtime for enhanced stability and support. If on Runtime 11.3 LTS or above, move directly to the latest 12.x version. If below, first migrate to 11.3 LTS, then to the latest 12.x version as per the migration guide.

controls.title: Recover from Structured Streaming query failures
controls.description: Structured Streaming ensures fault-tolerance and data consistency in streaming queries. With Azure Databricks workflows, you can set up your queries to automatically restart after failure, picking up precisely where they left off.

controls.title: Do not Store any Production Data in Default DBFS Folders
controls.description: Driven by security and data availability concerns, each Azure Databricks Workspace comes with a default DBFS designed for system-level artifacts like libraries and Init scripts, not for production data.

controls.title: Use a layered storage architecture
controls.description: Curate data by creating a layered architecture to increase data quality across layers. Start with a raw layer for ingested source data, continue with a curated layer for cleansed and refined data, and finish with a final layer catered to business needs, focusing on security and performance.

controls.title: Set up monitoring, alerting, and logging
controls.description: The Databricks Terraform provider is a flexible, powerful tool for managing Azure Databricks workspaces and cloud infrastructure.

controls.title: Enable autoscaling for SQL warehouse
controls.description: The scaling parameter of a SQL warehouse defines the min and max number of clusters for distributing queries. By default, it's set to one. Increasing the cluster count can accommodate more concurrent users effectively.

controls.title: Deploy workspaces in separate Subscriptions
controls.description: Customers often naturally divide workspaces by teams or departments. However, it's crucial to also consider Azure Subscription and Azure Databricks (ADB) Workspace limits when partitioning.

controls.title: Automatic Job Termination is enabled, ensure there are no user-defined local processes
controls.description: To conserve cluster resources, you can terminate a cluster to store its configuration for future reuse or autostart jobs. Clusters can auto-terminate after inactivity, but this only tracks Spark jobs, not local processes, which might still be running even after Spark jobs end.

wara.potential_benefits: Saves cluster resources, avoids idle use

controls.title: Automate deployments and workloads
controls.description: The Databricks Terraform provider manages Azure Databricks workspaces and cloud infrastructure flexibly and powerfully.

controls.title: Use a scalable and production-grade model serving infrastructure
controls.description: Use Databricks and MLflow for deploying models as Apache Spark UDFs, benefiting from job scheduling, retries, autoscaling, etc.

controls.title: Configure a disaster recovery pattern
controls.description:
Implementing a disaster recovery pattern is vital for Azure Databricks, ensuring data teams' access even during rare regional outages.

It is important to note that the Azure Databricks service is not entirely zone redudant and does support zonal failover.

controls.title: Use SSD backed VMs for Worker VM Type and Driver type
controls.description: Upgrade HDDs in premium VMs to SSDs for better speed and reliability. Premium SSDs boost IO-heavy apps; Standard SSDs balance cost and performance. Ideal for critical workloads, upgrading improves connectivity with brief reboot. Consider for vital VMs

controls.title: Enable autoscaling for batch workloads
controls.description: Autoscaling adjusts cluster sizes automatically based on workload demands, offering benefits for many use cases in terms of costs and performance. It includes guidance on when and how to best utilize Autoscaling. For streaming, Delta Live Tables with autoscaling is advised.

controls.title: Isolate each workspace in its own VNet
controls.description: Deploying only one Databricks Workspace per VNet aligns with Azure Databricks' isolation model.

controls.title: Automatically rescue invalid or nonconforming data with Databricks Auto Loader or Delta Live Tables
controls.description: Invalid or nonconforming data can crash workloads dependent on specific data formats. Best practices recommend filtering such data at ingestion to improve end-to-end resilience, ensuring no data is lost or missed.

controls.title: Enable Logging-Cluster log delivery
controls.description: When creating a Databricks cluster, you can set a log delivery location for the Spark driver, worker nodes, and events. Logs are delivered every 5 mins and archived hourly. Upon cluster termination, all generated logs until that point are guaranteed to be delivered.

controls.title: Configure jobs for automatic retries and termination
controls.description: Use Databricks and MLflow for deploying models as Spark UDFs for job scheduling, retries, autoscaling. Model serving offers scalable infrastructure, processes models using MLflow, and serves them via REST API using serverless compute managed in Databricks cloud.

controls.title: Evaluate regional isolation for workspaces
controls.description: Move workspaces to in-region control plane for increased regional isolation. Identify current control plane region using the workspace URL and nslookup. When region from CNAME differs from workspace region and an in-region control is available, consider migration using tools provided below.

controls.title: Create regular backups
controls.description: To recover from a failure, regular backups are needed. The Databricks Labs project migrate lets admins create backups by exporting workspace assets using the Databricks CLI/API. These backups help in restoring or migrating workspaces.

controls.title: Recover ETL jobs based on Delta time travel
controls.description: Despite thorough testing, a production job can fail or yield unexpected data. Sometimes, repairs are done by adding jobs post-issue identification and pipeline correction.

wara.potential_benefits: Easy rollback and fix for ETL jobs

controls.title: Use constraints and data expectations
controls.description: Delta tables verify data quality automatically with SQL constraints, triggering an error for violations. Delta Live Tables enhance this by defining expectations for data quality, utilizing Python or SQL, to manage actions for record failures, ensuring data integrity and compliance.

controls.title: Do not use Azure Spot VMs for critical Production workloads
controls.description: Azure Spot VMs are not suitable for critical production workloads needing high availability and reliability. They are meant for fault-tolerant tasks and can be evicted with 30-seconds notice if Azure needs the capacity, with no SLA guarantees.

controls.title: Actively manage schemas
controls.description: Uncontrolled schema changes can lead to invalid data and failing jobs. Databricks validates and enforces schema through Delta Lake, which prevents bad records during ingestion, and Auto Loader, which detects new columns and supports schema evolution to maintain data integrity.

wara.potential_benefits: Prevents invalid data and job failures

controls.title: Use Databricks Workflows and built-in recovery
controls.description: Databricks Workflows enable efficient error recovery in multi-task jobs by offering a matrix view for issue examination. Fixes can be applied to initiate repair runs targeting only failed and dependent tasks, preserving successful outcomes and thereby saving time and money.

wara.potential_benefits: Saves time and money with smart recovery

controls.title: Use Delta Live Tables enhanced autoscaling
controls.description: Databricks enhanced autoscaling optimizes cluster utilization by automatically allocating cluster resources based on workload volume, with minimal impact on the data processing latency of your pipelines.

wara.potential_benefits: Optimized resource use and minimal latency

controls.title: Use Delta Lake for higher reliability
controls.description: Delta Lake is an open source storage format enhancing data lakes' reliability with ACID transactions, schema enforcement, and scalable metadata handling.

controls.title: Improve data integrity by reducing data redundancy
controls.description: Copying data leads to redundancy, lost integrity, lineage, and access issues, affecting lakehouse data quality. Temporary copies are useful for agility and innovation but can become problematic operational data silos, questioning data's master status and currency.

controls.title: Use managed services where possible
controls.description: Where possible Leverage managed services (serverless compute) from the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform, such as:serverless SQL warehouses, model serving, serverless jobs, serverless compute for notebooks.

wara.potential_benefits: Improve resiliency and scalability at no additional cost

controls.title: Configure geo redundant backup storage
controls.description: Configure GRS to ensure that your database meets its availability and durability targets even in the face of failures or disasters.

wara.potential_benefits: Recover from regional failure and/or disaster
wara.learn_more_name: Backup and restore in Azure Database for MySQL - Flexible Server

controls.title: Configure storage auto-grow
controls.description: Configure storage auto-grow to prevent the server from running out of storage and becoming read-only.

wara.potential_benefits: Scale storage automatically to meet increasing demand
wara.learn_more_name: Azure Database for MySQL - Flexible Server service tiers - Storage auto grow

controls.title: Enable custom maintenance schedule
controls.description: Use custom maintenance schedule on flexible server instances to select a preferred time for service updates to be applied.

wara.learn_more_name: Scheduled maintenance in Azure Database for MySQL - Flexible Server

controls.title: Enable HA with zone redundancy
controls.description: Enable HA with zone redundancy on flexible server instances to deploy a standby replica in a different zone, offering automatic failover capability for improved reliability and disaster recovery.

wara.learn_more_name: High availability concepts in Azure Database for MySQL - Flexible Server

controls.title: Configure one or more read replicas
controls.description: Configure one or more read replicas to ensure that your database meets its availability and durability targets even in the face of failures or disasters.

wara.potential_benefits: Recover from regional failure and/or disaster
wara.learn_more_name: Read replicas in Azure Database for MySQL - Flexible Server

controls.title: Configure one or more read replicas
controls.description: Configure one or more read replicas to ensure that your database meets its availability and durability targets even in the face of failures or disasters.

wara.potential_benefits: Recover from regional failure and/or disaster
wara.learn_more_name: Read replicas in Azure Database for PostgreSQL - Flexible Server

controls.title: Configure geo redundant backup storage
controls.description: Configure GRS to ensure that your database meets its availability and durability targets even in the face of failures or disasters.

wara.potential_benefits: Recover from regional failure and/or disaster
wara.learn_more_name: Backup and restore in Azure Database for PostgreSQL - Flexible Server

controls.title: Configure storage auto-grow
controls.description: Configure storage auto-grow to prevent the server from running out of storage and becoming read-only.

wara.potential_benefits: Scale storage automatically to meet increasing demand
wara.learn_more_name: Storage autogrow using Azure portal in Azure Database for PostgreSQL - Flexible Server

controls.title: Enable custom maintenance schedule
controls.description: Use custom maintenance schedule on flexible server instances to select a preferred time for service updates to be applied.

wara.learn_more_name: Scheduled maintenance in Azure Database for PostgreSQL - Flexible Server

controls.title: Enable HA with zone redundancy
controls.description: Enable HA with zone redundancy on flexible server instances to deploy a standby replica in a different zone, offering automatic failover capability for improved reliability and disaster recovery.

wara.learn_more_name: Overview of high availability with Azure Database for PostgreSQL

controls.title: Create a validation host pool
controls.description: Validation host pools let you monitor service updates before the service applies them to your standard or non-validation environment.

wara.learn_more_name: Configure a host pool as a validation environment

controls.title: Use Azure Site Recovery to protect stateful session hosts
controls.description: Implement Azure Site Recovery (ASR) to replicate or backup stateful session hosts. This replicates VMs to a secondary Azure region or availability zone, ensuring recovery from a known VM state in case of an outage.

controls.title: Ensure a unique OU is used when deploying host pools with domain joined session hosts
controls.description: Place domain joined session hosts VMs in unique OUs. Segregate Prod and DR units for environment-specific settings. This ensures targeted configurations for session hosts, including FSLogix, session controls, etc.

wara.learn_more_name: Configure the VMs and install Active Directory Domain Services

controls.title: Configure host pool scheduled agent updates
controls.description: Create up to two maintenance windows for the Azure Virtual Desktop agent, side-by-side stack, and Geneva Monitoring agent to get updated so that updates don't happen during peak business hours.

wara.learn_more_name: Scheduled Agent Updates for Azure Virtual Desktop host pools

controls.title: Create scaling plans per region
controls.description: Scaling plans can only be assigned to host pools in the same region, on multi-region deployment scenario each region should has its own scaling plan.

wara.learn_more_name: Create and assign an autoscale scaling plan

controls.title: Define Failover Guidelines
controls.description: In case of a regional failure, an IoT Hub can failover to a second region, automatically or manually, to ensure your application continues working.

wara.learn_more_name: IoT Hub high availability and disaster recovery

controls.title: Use Availability Zones
controls.description: In regions supporting Availability Zones for IoT Hub, using these zones boosts availability. They're automatically activated for new IoT Hubs in supported areas.

wara.learn_more_name: Azure IoT Hub high availability and disaster recovery

controls.title: Device Identities are exported to a secondary region
controls.description: Device Identities should be copied to the failover region IoT Hub for all IoT devices to ensure connectivity in case of a failover. Manual Failover to another region is quicker (RTO), suitable for mission critical workloads.

wara.learn_more_name: Import and export IoT Hub device identities in bulk

controls.title: Use Device Provisioning Service
controls.description: Device Provisioning Service (DPS) enables easy redistribution of IoT devices for scaling and availability, allowing devices to be reassigned and not bound to specific IoT Hub instances. Devices in IoT Hubs using DPS should be verified for DPS utilization.

wara.learn_more_name: IoT Hub Device Provisioning Service (DPS) terminology

controls.title: Disabled Fallback Route
controls.description: Using message routing for custom endpoints in IoT Hub, messages might not reach these destinations if specific conditions are unmet. A default route ensures all messages are received, but disabling this safety net risks leaving some messages undelivered.

controls.title: Do not use free tier
controls.description: In a production scenario, the IoT Hub tier should not be Free because the Free tier does not provide the necessary Service Level Agreement.

wara.learn_more_name: Choose the right IoT Hub tier and size for your solution

controls.title: Configure at least two regions for high availability
controls.description: Enable a secondary region in Cosmos DB for higher SLA without downtime. Simple as pinning a location on a map. For Strong consistency, configure at least three regions for write availability in case of failure.

wara.learn_more_name: Distribute data globally with Azure Cosmos DB

controls.title: Maintain singleton pattern in your client
controls.description: Using a single instance of the SDK client for each account and application is crucial as connections are tied to the client. Compute environments have a limit on open connections, affecting connectivity when exceeded.

wara.learn_more_name: Designing resilient applications with Azure Cosmos DB SDKs

controls.title: Enable availability zones
controls.description: When availability zones are configured, Azure Cosmos DB intelligently distributes the 4 replicas of your data across all available zones. It ensures that your Azure Cosmos DB can withstand an outage in one availability zone and remain fully operational throughout.

wara.learn_more_name: High availability in Azure Cosmos DB

controls.title: Enable service-managed failover for multi-region accounts with single write region
controls.description: Cosmos DB boasts high uptime and resiliency. Even so, issues may arise. With Service-Managed failover, if a region is down, Cosmos DB automatically switches to the next available region, requiring no user action.

wara.learn_more_name: Manage an Azure Cosmos DB account by using the Azure portal

controls.title: Evaluate multi-region write capability
controls.description: Multi-region writes enable high availability but require careful consistency and conflict resolution. Using Bounded Staleness is an anti-pattern, as replication lag increases latency and coordination overhead. This setup undermines scalability, impacting performance and availability.

wara.learn_more_name: Distribute data globally with Azure Cosmos DB

controls.title: Ensure query results are fully drained
controls.description: Cosmos DB has a 4 MB response limit, leading to paginated results for large or partition-spanning queries. Each page shows availability and provides a continuation token for the next. A while loop in code is necessary to traverse all pages until completion.

controls.title: Monitor Cosmos DB health and set up alerts
controls.description: Monitoring the availability and responsiveness of Azure Cosmos DB resources and having alerts set up for your workload is a good practice. This ensures you stay proactive in handling unforeseen events.

wara.learn_more_name: Create alerts for Azure Cosmos DB using Azure Monitor

controls.title: Configure continuous backup mode
controls.description: Cosmos DB's backup is always on, offering protection against data mishaps. Continuous mode allows for self-serve restoration to a pre-mishap point, unlike periodic mode which requires contacting Microsoft support, leading to longer restore times.

wara.learn_more_name: Continuous backup with point in time restore feature in Azure Cosmos DB

controls.title: Implement retry logic in your client
controls.description: Cosmos DB SDKs automatically manage many transient errors through retries. Despite this, it's crucial for applications to implement additional retry policies targeting specific cases that the SDKs can't generically address, ensuring more robust error handling.

wara.learn_more_name: Designing resilient applications with Azure Cosmos DB SDKs

controls.title: Configure Diagnostic Settings for all Azure Event Grid resources
controls.description: Enabling diagnostic settings on Azure Event Grid resources like custom topics, system topics, and domains lets you capture and view diagnostic information to troubleshoot failures effectively.

wara.learn_more_name: Azure Event Grid - Enable diagnostic logs for Event Grid resources

controls.title: Configure Dead-letter to save events that cannot be delivered
controls.description: Event Grid may not deliver an event within a specific time or after several attempts, leading to dead-lettering where undelivered events are sent to a storage account.

wara.learn_more_name: Azure Event Grid delivery and retry

controls.title: Azure Event Grid topics should use Private Link Private Endpoints
controls.description: Use private endpoints for secure event ingress to custom topics/domains via a private link, avoiding the public internet. It employs an IP from the VNet space for your topic/domain.

wara.learn_more_name: Configure private endpoints for Azure Event Grid topics or domains

controls.title: Ensure zone redundancy is enabled in supported regions
controls.description: When using the Azure portal, zone redundancy is automatically enabled. However, some Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tools may default this to false. To ensure replication of metadata and events across data centers in an availability zone, always verify that zone redundancy is enabled.

wara.potential_benefits: Enhanced fault tolerance for Event Hub

controls.title: Enable auto-inflate on Event Hub Standard tier
controls.description: Enable auto-inflate on Event Hub Standard tier namespaces to automatically scale up throughput units (TUs), meeting usage needs and preventing data ingress or egress throttle scenarios by adjusting to allowed rates.

wara.learn_more_name: Azure Event Hubs - Automatically scale throughput units

controls.title: Configure Resource Health Alerts
controls.description: Configure Resource Health Alerts for all applicable resources to stay informed about the current and historical health status of your Azure resources. They notify you when these resources have a change in their health status.

controls.title: Migrate from Application Insights instrumentation keys to connection strings
controls.description: Application Insights is changing from global ingestion endpoints to regional endpoints that use connection strings. Connection strings make telemetry ingestion more reliable by removing dependencies on global ingestion endpoints. Transition to connection string-based ingestion before 31 March 2025.

wara.learn_more_name: Migrate from Application Insights instrumentation keys to connection strings

controls.title: Convert Classic Deployments
controls.description: Classic Application Insights retires in February 2024. To minimize disruption to existing application monitoring scenarios, transition to workspace-based Application Insights before 29 February 2024.

wara.learn_more_name: Migrate an Application Insights classic resource to a workspace-based resource

controls.title: Private endpoint should be configured for Key Vault
controls.description: Azure Private Link Service lets you securely and privately connect to Azure Key Vault via a Private Endpoint in your VNet, using a private IP and eliminating public Internet exposure.

wara.potential_benefits: Secure Key Vault with Private Link
wara.learn_more_name: Azure Key Vault Private Link Service overview

controls.title: Key vaults should have soft delete enabled
controls.description: Key Vault's soft-delete feature enables recovery of deleted vaults and objects like keys, secrets, and certificates. When enabled, marked resources are retained for 90 days, allowing for their recovery, essentially undoing deletion.

controls.title: Diagnostic logs in Key Vault should be enabled
controls.description: Enable logs, set up alerts, and adhere to retention requirements for improved monitoring and security of Key Vault access, detailing the frequency and identity of users.

controls.title: Key vaults should have purge protection enabled
controls.description: Purge protection secures against malicious deletions by enforcing a retention period for soft deleted key vaults, ensuring no one, not even insiders or Microsoft, can purge your key vaults during this period, preventing permanent data loss.

wara.potential_benefits: Protects from insider attacks, avoids data loss

controls.title: Use separate key vaults per application per environment
controls.description: Key vaults are security boundaries for secret storage. Grouping secrets together increases risk during a security event, as attacks could access multiple secrets.

wara.learn_more_name: Azure Key Vault best practices overview

controls.title: Create the Azure machine learning registry in multiple regions
controls.description: Azure Machine Learning registries enables to create and use assets (models, env, components, and datasets) in different workspaces. Registries support multi-region replication for low latency access to assets, allowing to use them in workspaces located in different Azure regions.

controls.title: Ensure to create Machine Learning Compute resources in secondary region
controls.description: Create compute resources for training a Machine Learning model in selected regions. Ensure both regions have sufficient compute quota for dynamic scaling. Customers must configure HA across zones for attached compute resources like AKS, Azure Databricks, Container Instances.

wara.learn_more_name: Failover for business continuity and disaster recovery

controls.title: Make Azure Machine Learning quota requests through the Azure Machine Learning Studio
controls.description: Requests for additional Azure Machine Learning quota should be made through the Azure Machine Learning Studio instead of the subscription level in the Azure portal.

wara.learn_more_name: Manage and increase quotas and limits for resources with Azure Machine Learning

controls.title: Deploy Azure Machine learning workspace in secondary region
controls.description: If your primary workspace is unavailable, switch to the secondary workspace to continue work. Azure Machine Learning doesn't auto-submit jobs to the secondary workspace during an outage. Update your code configuration to point to the new workspace resource.

wara.learn_more_name: Failover for business continuity and disaster recovery

controls.title: Choose SKUs with longer terms and avoid those nearing retirement
controls.description: When choosing SKUs, opt for those that support longer terms and steer clear of any SKUs that are nearing retirement. This ensures that you can continue to use the SKU for a longer period of time.

wara.learn_more_name: What are compute targets in Azure Machine Learning

controls.title: Selecting regions for BCDR, ensure that both regions offer adequate compute quotas
controls.description: When selecting regions for BCDR, ensure that both regions offer adequate compute quotas to meet your requirements in the same SKU. This ensures that you can failover to the secondary region without any issues.

wara.potential_benefits: Provide enough compute resources to the secondary region

controls.title: Ensure checkpoints are used for AI training models
controls.description: Checkpoint optimization for large model training is crucial for disaster recovery. It reduces training time, increases reliability, improves cost efficiency, enhances resource utilization, and supports scalability by saving model states periodically to resume training from the last saved point.

wara.potential_benefits: Reduces costs, training time and increases reliability.

controls.title: Plan for a multi-regional deployment of Azure Machine Learning and associated resources
controls.description: Ensure you have a recovery strategy defined. Check regional availability and paired regions. Machine Learning doesn't have auto failover. Therefore, you must design a strategy that encompasses the workspace and all its dependencies, such as Key Vault, Azure Storage, and Container Registry.

controls.title: Avoid NC and NC_Promo series Azure VMs for machine learning quotas; migrate to newer versions
controls.description: Avoid selecting NC and NC_Promo series Azure virtual machines for machine learning VM quotas and make sure to migrate to newer versions.

wara.potential_benefits: Avoid service disruption, longer term support
wara.learn_more_name: Migration Guide for GPU Compute Workloads in Azure

controls.title: Monitor Azure NetApp Files metrics to better understand usage pattern and performance
controls.description: Azure NetApp Files offers metrics like allocated storage, actual usage, volume IOPS, and latency, enabling a better understanding of usage patterns and volume performance for NetApp accounts.

wara.learn_more_name: Ways to monitor Azure NetApp Files | Microsoft Learn

controls.title: Use availability zones for high availability in Azure NetApp Files
controls.description: Availability zones are distinct locations within an Azure region to withstand local failures. Deploy your workload in multiple availability zones and use application-based replication or Azure NetApp Files cross-zone replication to achieve high availability. Note that failover is a manual process.

wara.learn_more_name: Use availability zones for high availability in Azure NetApp Files | Microsoft Learn

controls.title: Ensure application resilience for service maintenance events
controls.description: Azure NetApp Files might undergo occasional planned maintenance such as platform updates or service and software upgrades. It's important to be aware of the application's resiliency settings to cope with these storage service maintenance events.

wara.learn_more_name: What do you recommend for handling potential application disruptions due to storage service maintenance events? | Microsoft Learn

controls.title: Enforce standards and assess compliance in Azure NetApp Files with Azure policy
controls.description: Azure NetApp Files supports Azure policy integration using either built-in policy definitions or by creating custom ones to maintain organizational standards and compliance.

wara.learn_more_name: Azure Policy definitions for Azure NetApp Files | Microsoft Learn

controls.title: Use snapshots for data protection in Azure NetApp Files
controls.description: Azure NetApp Files snapshot technology ensures stability, scalability, and swift data recoverability without affecting performance. It supports automatic snapshot creation via policies for Azure NetApp Files data.

wara.potential_benefits: Stable, scalable, swift recovery, no perf impact
wara.learn_more_name: How Azure NetApp Files snapshots work | Microsoft Learn

controls.title: Deploy ANF volumes in the same availability zone with Azure compute and other services
controls.description: Azure NetApp Files' availability zone (AZ) volume placement feature lets you deploy volumes in the same AZ with Azure compute and other services to have within AZ latency and share the same AZ failure domain.

wara.potential_benefits: Within AZ latency and tolerate failure of other AZ
wara.learn_more_name: Manage availability zone volume placement for Azure NetApp Files | Microsoft Learn

controls.title: Use standard network features for production in Azure NetApp Files
controls.description: Standard network feature in Azure NetApp Files enhances IP limits and VNet capabilities, including network security groups, user-defined routes on subnets, and diverse connectivity options.

wara.learn_more_name: Guidelines for Azure NetApp Files network planning | Microsoft Learn

controls.title: Use the correct service level and volume quota size for the expected performance level
controls.description: Service levels, part of capacity pool attributes, determine the maximum throughput per volume quota in Azure NetApp Files. It combines read and write speed, offering three levels: Standard (16 MiB/s per 1TiB), Premium (64 MiB/s per 1TiB), and Ultra (128 MiB/s per 1TiB) throughput.

wara.learn_more_name: Service levels for Azure NetApp Files | Microsoft Learn

controls.title: Enable backup for data protection in Azure NetApp Files
controls.description: Azure NetApp Files offers a fully managed backup solution enhancing long-term recovery, archiving, and compliance.

wara.learn_more_name: Understand Azure NetApp Files backup | Microsoft Learn

controls.title: Restrict default access to Azure NetApp Files volumes
controls.description: Access to the delegated subnet should be limited to specific Azure Virtual Networks. SMB-enabled volumes' share permissions should move away from 'Everyone/Full control'. NFS-enabled volumes' access needs to be controlled via export policies and/or NFSv4.1 ACLs.

wara.potential_benefits: Enhanced security, Reduced data breach risk
wara.learn_more_name: Configure network features for an Azure NetApp Files volume

controls.title: Make use of SMB continuous availability for supported applications
controls.description: Certain SMB applications need SMB Transparent Failover for maintenance without interrupting server connectivity. Azure NetApp Files provides this through SMB Continuous Availability for applications like Citrix App Layering, FSLogix user/profile containers, Microsoft SQL Server, MSIX app attach.

wara.learn_more_name: Do I need to take special precautions for SMB-based applications? | Microsoft Learn

controls.title: Enable Cross-region replication of Azure NetApp Files volumes
controls.description: Azure NetApp Files replication offers data protection by allowing asynchronous cross-region volume replication for application failover in case of regional outages. Volumes can be replicated across regions, not concurrently with cross-zone replication. Note that failover is a manual process.

wara.potential_benefits: Enhanced data protection and disaster recovery
wara.learn_more_name: Cross-region replication of Azure NetApp Files volumes

controls.title: Enable Cross-zone replication of Azure NetApp Files volumes
controls.description: The cross-zone replication (CZR) feature enables asynchronous data replication between Azure NetApp Files volumes across different availability zones, ensuring data protection and critical application failover in case of zone-wide disasters. Note that failover is a manual process.

wara.potential_benefits: Enhances disaster recovery across availability zones
wara.learn_more_name: Cross-zone replication of Azure NetApp Files volumes | Microsoft Learn

controls.title: Plan for backend maintenance by using connection draining
