controls.title: Ensure that each SAP production system is designed for high availability across availability zones
controls.description: Use Azure Availability Zones to protect SAP systems against data center failures. Ensure high availability by deploying across multiple zones. If deployment across zones isn't possible, refer to Microsoft's guidance for high availability options for SAP workloads.

wara.learn_more_name: High Availability Deployment Options for SAP

controls.title: If using single-instance VMs all OS and data disks must be Premium SSD or Ultra Disk
controls.description: For single-instance VMs, both OS and data disks must be either Premium SSD or Ultra Disk to achieve the single-instance SLA of 99.9% availability.

controls.title: Ensure there is a robust monitoring and alerting solution in place for the entire DR solution
controls.description: Implement robust monitoring and alerting for SAP on Azure, covering DR for databases, central services, applications, and shared file systems. Given SAP's complexity, a comprehensive monitoring strategy is crucial for effective DR replication and rapid issue response.

wara.potential_benefits: Improved DR oversight and rapid issue response

controls.title: Document and test DR procedure ensure it meets RPO and RTO targets
controls.description: Document DR procedures for each SAP layer: database, central services, application servers, and shared file systems. Include configuration, failover mechanisms, and recovery steps. Test various failure scenarios to ensure the DR strategy meets RPO/RTO targets and provides seamless failover.

controls.title: Design SAP shared file systems for high availability, utilizing availability zones when possible
controls.description:
SAP shared file systems such as /sapmnt, /usr/trans, interfaces should be made highly available.
In case of Azure File Shares, we recommend that you use ZRS (Zone-redundant storage) and for Azure NetApp Files use Zonal replication for your volumes.

controls.title: SAP shared files systems are replicated or backed up to DR location
controls.description: Implement robust monitoring and alerting for DR in SAP on Azure to cover its complex, multi-layer architecture. This is crucial for databases, services, applications, and shared systems.

controls.title: Replicate production databases to DR location (ASYNC) using the vendor's replication technology
controls.description: Replicate production databases (ASYNC) to the DR location using the database vendor's replication technology.

controls.title: RE:04 Define reliability and recovery targets
controls.description: Define reliability and recovery targets for the components, the flows, and the overall solution. Use the defined targets to build the health model. The health model defines what healthy, degraded, and unhealthy states look like.

controls.title: RE:06 Design for reliable scaling
controls.description: Implement a timely and reliable scaling strategy at the application, data, and infrastructure levels.

controls.title: RE:05 Design for high availability with availability zones
controls.description: High availability is a foundational tenet of designing for reliability. A highly available architecture can help you avoid downtime as much as possible and recover efficiently if downtime does occur.

controls.title: RE:07 Use background jobs
controls.description: Background jobs help minimize the load on the application UI, which improves availability and reduces interactive response time.

controls.title: RE:09 Implement business continuity and disaster recovery plan
controls.description: Implement structured, tested, and documented business continuity and disaster recovery (BCDR) plans that align with the recovery targets. Plans must cover all components and the system as a whole.

controls.title: RE:07 Handle transient faults
controls.description: Build capabilities into the solution by using infrastructure-based reliability patterns and software-based design patterns to handle component failures and transient errors.

controls.title: RE:02 Identify and rate user and system flows
controls.description: Identify and rate user and system flows. Use a criticality scale based on your business requirements to prioritize the flows.

controls.title: RE:07 Implement self-preservation and self-healing measures
controls.description: Strengthen the resiliency and recoverability of your workload by implementing self-preservation and self-healing measures. Self-healing capabilities help you avoid downtime by building in failure detection and automatic corrective actions to respond to different failure types.

controls.title: RE:08 Design a reliability testing strategy
controls.description: Test resiliency and availability scenarios by applying the principles of chaos engineering in your test and production environments. Use testing to ensure that your graceful degradation implementation and scaling strategies are effective by performing active malfunction and simulated load testing.

controls.title: RE:06 Design for data partitioning
controls.description: Partitioning data improves scalability, reduces contention, and optimizes performance. Implement data partitioning to divide data by usage pattern.

controls.title: RE:01 Design your workload to align with business objectives
controls.description: Design your workload to align with business objectives and avoid unnecessary complexity or overhead. Use a practical and balanced approach to make design decisions that deliver the desired results. Contain your design to the necessities to reduce inefficiencies and potential problems.

controls.title: RE:10 Design a reliable monitoring and alerting strategy
controls.description: Measure and publish the solution's health indicators. Continuously capture uptime and other reliability data from across the workload and also from individual components and key flows.

controls.title: RE:05 Design for multi-region high availability
controls.description: High availability is a foundational tenet of designing for reliability. A highly available architecture can help you avoid downtime as much as possible and recover efficiently if downtime does occur.

controls.title: RE:05 Design for redundancy
controls.description: Add redundancy at different levels, especially for critical flows. Apply redundancy to the compute, data, network, and other infrastructure tiers in accordance with the identified reliability targets.

controls.title: RE:03 Use failure mode analysis to identify and prioritize potential failures
controls.description: Use failure mode analysis (FMA) to identify and prioritize potential failures in your solution components. Perform FMA to help you assess the risk and effect of each failure mode. Determine how the workload responds and recovers.
